overview: Black sacrifices a pawn immediately with 2...Qh4, hoping for a quick attack on f2 and traps. White can simply play 3.g3 Qxe5 and keeps an extra pawn with a comfortable position. It is a joke-level line that scores only through surprise.

white_ideas.idea: Keep the pawn and develop with g3, Nf3 and Bg2

black_ideas.idea: Win the pawn back with ...Qxe5 and ...Nc6
Hope for tactics against f2 or the e-pawn

typical_structures.structure: White extra pawn on e5, Black queen out early

character.notes: Black risks everything on an early queen sortie, so one wrong move loses quickly.

gambit.notes: Black gives the e-pawn and White can keep it.

soundness.notes: Strong players consider it unsound, like the main Englund Gambit.

structure.notes: The e-pawn exchange opens the centre immediately.

approach.notes: Almost never played by strong players.
